notes.1: Most candidates were successful in obtaining the critical values associated with the inequality, either by a pair of correct linear equations or a quadratic equation (ignoring inequality signs). However, fewer candidates then obtained a correct domain.
notes.2: Many candidates were unable to expand out sin ( θ+30o) correctly even though the form of this expansion is in the formula booklet provided. Some candidates did not recall that cosecθ= . There were two sinθ approaches which could be adopted for answering this question. The more common approach was to  3 1  1 expand out  sinθ+ cosθ× in order to obtain an equation in terms of cotθ and hence an   2 2   sinθ equation in tanθ, which could then be solved. Errors in the expansion of these two terms were common, mainly due to algebraic errors, but many candidates were then able to solve their equation in tanθ, to obtain at least one solution. The second approach was to multiply each side of the equation by sinθ and then simplify the resulting equation to obtain an equation in tanθ.
notes.3a: Few correct responses were seen. Most candidates were able to expand (secx+cosx)2 to obtain sec2x+cos2x+2. Few candidates recognised the need to use the double angle formula to write 1+cos2x cos2x as . In many cases, the power of 2 in the cosine term became a coefficient of the cosine term so that the given form appeared to be obtained. The incorrect response of sec2x+2+cos2x was the most common solution given by candidates.
notes.3b: Many candidates were able to obtain method marks, even though an incorrect solution had been given for part (a), by integrating sec2x and cos2x correctly and then attempting a correct substitution of limits. For those candidates with completely correct solutions, the final accuracy 9709 Mathematics June 2021 mark was sometimes not awarded as the final answer was not given in exact form, as required by the question. Candidates should ensure that they check the question to ensure that they have given their final answer in the required form.
notes.4a: Several candidates demonstrated good knowledge of the basic properties of logarithms and hence a correct value for the parameter was usually obtained. However, many candidates were unable to 2t+6 write ln ( 2t+6 )−lnt as ln . Many candidates also attempted to differentiate the expressions for x and y, with respect to t, without reading the question carefully enough. Many correct derivatives were seen in this question part, with the calculation for finding the value of t not always being included.
notes.4b: Few correct responses were seen. Errors included the incorrect differentiation of ln ( 2t+6 ) as 1 2 dy rather than the correct . Some candidates did not recognise that to find , 2t+6 2t+6 dt differentiation of a product was needed. An exact answer was needed to this question, which many candidates did not show.
notes.5a: Use of the quotient rule was widely recognised and applied correctly. However, misuse of brackets and incorrect simplification of (lnx)2 were common. Many candidates were able to confirm the final result correctly.
notes.5b: Very few correct methods of solution were seen. Many candidates realised that they were looking for a change of sign when considering the value of a function when the two given values were 3x+2 3x+2 substituted. Most candidates considered the function needed to be rather than x− 3lnx 3lnx or equivalent. Other methods are acceptable provided a full explanation is given.
notes.5c: Most candidates who attempted this question part were able to obtain a correct result to the required accuracy.
notes.6a: Many candidates had difficulty calculating the correct width of the trapezia and hence obtained an incorrect number of incorrect y values.
notes.6b: A large number of completely correct answers were seen although an exact answer was required for this question. Provided a correct exact answer was seen using a correct integral, candidates obtained the full marks available even if the exact answer was subsequently evaluated.
notes.6c: Most candidates recognised that a subtraction of the answers obtained in the two previous parts of the question was needed.
notes.6d: Few candidates were able to give a correct answer together with a correct reason. Reasons usually concerned numerical accuracy rather than the shape of the curve and relative trapezia.
notes.7a: Most candidates were able to use the factor theorem correctly and obtain a correct answer.
notes.7b: Correct factorisation was usually seen. Most candidates were able to divide by x – 3 either algebraically or by synthetic division in order to obtain the correct quadratic factor. Most continued to obtain the correct three linear factors.
notes.7c: Most candidates recognised the connection between the demand of the question and the work done in the previous part, as implied by the use of the word ‘Hence’. Many then proceeded to work, incorrectly, with logarithmic functions rather than recognise a potential quadratic equation.
notes.general_comments:
Some candidates had clearly not prepared well or revised sufficiently for the examination as evidenced by
questions that were not attempted. Of those candidates who did attempt all the questions, showing a
reasonable understanding of the syllabus, there did not appear to be any issues with time.
